emily: hey everyone, first day here. trying to get a single dev setup (python/node/go/rust) on an Intel MBP. using asdf but python build keeps failing with openssl/linker errors. any short checklist or tricks?

devex: welcome! :wave: short checklist for intel macs: brew, asdf (+plugins), pkg-config, openssl@1.1, git, 1password cli, docker, direnv. for python builds you usually need to point CPython at brew's openssl.

sam: exact flags that fixed it for me:
```bash
brew install openssl@1.1 pkg-config
export BREW_OPENSSL_DIR="$(brew --prefix openssl@1.1)"
export CFLAGS="-I${BREW_OPENSSL_DIR}/include"
export LDFLAGS="-L${BREW_OPENSSL_DIR}/lib"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="${BREW_OPENSSL_DIR}/lib/pkgconfig"
export PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS="--with-openssl=${BREW_OPENSSL_DIR}"
asdf plugin-add python || true
asdf install python 3.11.5
```
That PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS helps when you have mixed /opt/homebrew and /usr/local leftovers.

emily: nice, thanks. nodejs plugin wants gpg?

kevin: yes, `brew install gpg` and follow asdf-nodejs docs to import the release team's keys. one-time step. after node install i do `npm i -g corepack && corepack enable` so yarn/pnpm behave consistently.

emily: .tool-versions & dotfiles etiquette?

devex: policy: commit repo-level .tool-versions. keep machine-only pins in `~/.tool-versions-local` in your dotfiles and don't commit it. put `eval "$(asdf init -)"` in your shell rc. use direnv/.envrc per-project for env vars, not global shell exports.

emily: how to manage REDWOOD_API_KEY for local dev?

sam: request access to the "Redwood - Developer Secrets" 1Password vault. then use op cli in your .envrc: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$(op item get "redwood/staging-api-key" --fields label=secret)"`. direnv autoloads it per repo.

emily: ssh/gpg commit signing and forwarding tips?

kevin: generate ed25519 ssh key, add to GitHub, `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. ssh config: `AddKeysToAgent yes`, `UseKeychain yes`, `ForwardAgent yes`. for GPG signing, generate a key and set `git config --global user.signingkey <keyid>` and `git config --global commit.gpgsign true`. if you prefer, you can use GitHub's SSH commit signing too.

emily: any way to avoid long CPython compiles?

devex: options: use prebuilt wheels via a devcontainer image, use infra's shared builder VM, or accept one-time build cost and cache via asdf local package caches. if you want totally hermetic, use a devcontainer with the exact tool versions.

emily: thanks all, the PYTHON_CONFIGURE_OPTS approach worked. will set up node + corepack next and ping if stuck. :raised_hands:

setup-bot: reminder: new hires should request 1Password vault access if not yet granted.
